scope: Proposition 4.2 (Rough propagation and path tails) of the manuscript “Cutoff throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase” (preprints/Cutoff-throughout-the-high-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-phase-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d99d391c8c3ed79f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 25-26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are constants C, c > 0 such that, for every vector function p, (∂t − L) ∥Ktp∥2 ≤ C ∥Ktp∥2 − c ∑︂ j wj ∥djKtp∥2 . (4.5) 25 In particular, for every starting law ν and t ≥ 0, Eν ∥Ktp∥2 ≤ eCt EνSt ∥p∥2 . (4.6) The same assertions hold with the multiplication term ap in Equation (4.2) replaced by zap, for each fixed real z. Expand in that multiplication term. Given H > 0, there are AH, BH < ∞ such that, for t ≥ 1, deleting terms with more than AHt insertions, and then clipping elementary likelihoods at exp(BHt), changes the resulting map by at most CHe−Ht as a map from L2(νSt; Rn) to L2(ν; Rn). The constants are uniform in ν, including point masses. Columnwise the same statement holds for Hilbert–Schmidt norms. For every fixed t > 0, sending the insertion cutoff and then the likelihood cap to infinity likewise gives convergence in this same all-vector-field operator bound. At t = 0 the map is the identity.
